_comment: One of the twelve plain colours, and it sets **every** colour there is to set.
`colour` is one name on eight aspects -- the vault, the air, the clouds over it, the star this world
goes round, the curtain over its cold, the bow opposite its sun, and the grass and the leaves that grow
in it. Each holds exactly one colour, so the name needs no prefix and attachment decides which is
meant: `red sky` paints the vault, `red clouds` what sails over it, `red sun` the star, `red and green
aurora` the ramp from its crown to its hem, and `a red Age` means all of them at once.
It declares no aspects: `Word.aspects` is widened from the parameters a word sets, so the `sets` map is
The light is deliberately *not* among them, which is why `tint` is still named apart. Saying the light
here is red is a different claim from saying the sky is, and `witchlight` is the idiom that makes it.
Aimed at the land it asks for a stone of its colour (`#white`, preset_tags/materials.json): dyed
concrete and terracotta, and what the world already makes in it. Laid bare, only one Age in ten is
built of it, so a plain coloured Age is not a world of concrete.
